description: Generated from schemas/commands/catalog.json. The MCP server (stdio) lists those of these tools that the running version implements (ADR-0009). $refs point into the top-level $defs; the server sends each tool schema with only the definitions it uses.

activity.title: Activity file
activity.description: `activity.json` in the cache folder of the working copy (ADR-0008): the last call through the local API or the MCP server that read or changed one element of the copy (SR-117). Every API and MCP process of the copy rewrites it after such a call (the last writer wins); the app watches it. It is internal and private (mode 0600, like `api.json`): scripts ask `workspace.activity`, which gives `access`. It holds no element content, only the UUID, repository, command, time and the hash of the element's file. Removing it is safe.

process.description: The writer: its process ID and 8 random hex digits, new whenever a workspace of the process starts recording. With `seq` it tells a new access from one already seen.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the element's file as the call left it, so that a reader can tell whether it sees that state of the file yet.

access.description: One call that read or changed one element: which access made it, the command, its effect, when it ended and the element.
The access the call came through (ADR-0002 rule 4). Only calls through the API and the MCP server are recorded.

command.description: The catalog command of the call.

effect.description: The effect of the command in the catalog.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element's file.

api-endpoint.title: API endpoint file
api-endpoint.description: `api.json` in the cache folder of the working copy (`<OS cache>/logreq/<sha256 of the absolute workspace root>/`, ADR-0008): where the running local API of `logreq serve api` listens, and its token (ADR-0009). Written at start with mode 0600; a client reads it and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The API listens on loopback only (SR-079). A file left behind by a stopped API names a port nobody listens on.

token.description: 256 random bits, base64url without padding; new at every start.

urls.description: Base URLs, one per loopback address the API listens on (`::1` only where the machine has IPv6).

pid.description: Process ID of the API. While it runs, a second API for the same working copy asks the URLs before it starts; when it does not run, the file is stale and is replaced.

baseline.title: Baseline file
baseline.description: A baseline is a YAML file with name, date, the commit of every repository involved and ID plus version of every element in the selection (D-039, SR-050). LogReq writes the file; a person commits it with Git (D-036, SR-050 AK4). No reason or approval field (D-006, SR-050 AK3). The metamodel of the baseline is given by the commit of the metamodel repository (D-021).

selection.description: How the elements were selected, for information. The element list is authoritative.

elements.description: Sorted by id; one flow mapping per line.

common.title: Shared definitions
common.description: Building blocks used by all LogReq file formats and commands. See docs/adr/0004 and 0005.

uuid.description: Element ID: random UUID version 4, lower case, never changes (D-017, SR-002).

shortId.description: Display ID: type prefix, dash, the trailing hex characters of the UUID with dashes removed, at least 6, more until unique in the workspace (D-017, SR-002 AK3). The file name uses 12 (D-056).

elementRef.description: UUID, short ID or identifier (e.g. SR-036), any case; several matches give ref.ambiguous.

uuidRef.description: A UUID version 4 as a caller gives it, in any case; the tool stores it in lower case (spec question #316).

elementId.description: A reference to an element as the tool writes it in outputs: UUID or short ID in their canonical form.

elementName.description: How an output names an element it gives elsewhere by UUID only (#588), for people: its short ID, its identifier when it has one (#305) and its title, as element.list gives them.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

version.description: Fassung: normal-form version, colon, first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 over the canonical content (D-013, D-027, ADR-0005). Example: n1:9f86d081884c7d65.

fileSha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes of an element file, lower-case hex: a write precondition, never stored and not a version (ADR-0005).

key.description: Fixed metamodel key of a type, property, relation kind or status value. Readable English, lower case, dashes (D-043, SR-010 AK2).

keyOrName.description: A metamodel value as a person gives it: its key or its display name, in any case (`Obsolete` names the status obsolete). The tool stores the key (SR-012 AK3).

relationTarget.description: Target of a relation as stored in the source file (D-013, D-058, SR-005, SR-021). Within the same repository: `id`, `version`, `title`. Across repositories: `id`, `version`, `repository` (workspace name of the target's repository), never title or text (D-058). Written as one flow mapping per line (SR-102, ADR-0004).

repository.description: Workspace name of the target's repository; required across repositories (D-058), absent within one.

relationTargetInput.description: Target of a relation as a caller gives it to element.create or element.update (SR-021). Only `id` and, across repositories, `repository` name the target. A target the property already stores keeps its stored version and form; for every other target the tool writes its current version and the title (same repository) or repository (across repositories) itself. A given `version` or `title` is ignored (spec question #177).

repository.description: Workspace name of the target's repository; absent for the source's own repository.

item.description: The item under test (Prüfling): the concrete build or sample that was checked. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

dateTime.description: A date and time with time zone (RFC 3339 date-time), for example 2026-10-26T09:30:00Z.

commit.description: Full Git object ID (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

relativePath.description: Path relative to the repository or file it appears in, forward slashes, no `..` segments.

localPath.description: A file or folder on the local machine, relative or absolute. CLI: relative to the current folder (the CLI makes it absolute before the call); API and MCP: relative to the workspace root (ADR-0009).

problem.description: A finding or hint. Commands return problems as data so every access shows the same result (SR-080).

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository the problem is about (element files of several repositories, the metamodel repository, a repository Git cannot read); `file`, when given, is relative to that repository.

elementRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element the problem is about, when `repository` and `file` name another file (the evidence record of `evidence.outdated`, SR-025 AK4). With `elementFile` it names one copy of a UUID several files share (SR-088).

elementFile.description: The file of the element the problem is about, relative to `elementRepository`; given with it.

elementShortId.description: Short ID of the element `elementId` names, for display (SR-002 AK3); given on every problem that names an element of the workspace, by every command that has read the elements.

elementIdentifier.description: Identifier of the element `elementId` names (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, #305), for display next to `elementShortId`; given with it when the element has one.

hintId.description: Stable ID of a confirmable hint (D-042); on the hint.* problems of hint.confirm, the ID as given.

problemCode.description: Stable codes. New codes are added here first, in the PR that needs them.

error.description: Error of a command call. Same codes over CLI (stderr, exit code), API (HTTP body) and MCP (tool error). `command.not-implemented`: the command is in the catalog, but this version does not implement it yet (a later stage).

incomplete.description: True when a result is incomplete because targets are in repositories that are not available locally (SR-006 AK2, SR-036 AK3).

selection.description: Which elements a command works on: a saved filter, an inline filter, a package, a baseline or explicit IDs, optionally seen through a variant view.

baseline.description: Name of a baseline, or its file name in the baselines folder (with or without .yaml). Not every command takes it yet.

viewId.description: A view as the tool writes it in outputs: `core` or the canonical UUID or short ID of a variant (SR-043).

view.description: `core`, a variant ID, or absent for all elements (SR-043).

verificationStatus.description: SR-031, SR-034. `indirect` = indirectly verified via children.

data-export.title: Data of a state (Stand) as JSON
data-export.description: Output of `data.export` and the file `<commit>.json` (or `<commit>-dirty.json`) that `data.store` writes (SR-061, SR-062) for external evaluation tools such as Grafana or DuckDB (D-008). Also defines the element and relation shapes all commands return.

generated.description: Time of the export, UTC, in seconds.

selection.description: The selection as given; left out when none was given (every element).

commit.description: HEAD of the repository, as `workspace.status` gives it; left out when Git cannot tell.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes, by content against `commit`, to the files the data is made of (workspace file, YAML files of the metamodel, filter and baseline folders, element files and the files they embed, also ones Git ignores; not evidence records); left out when Git cannot tell.

incomplete.description: A repository of the workspace is not on this machine (SR-006 AK2): its elements and the records of its evidence locations are missing. A baselines folder that is not on this machine holds no baseline: `selection.baseline` then gives `input.invalid`.

elements.description: Every element of the selection in workspace order, superseded ones included (D-045), without text; in data.export each with `validity`, `packages`, `verification` and its relations with `currentVersion` and `outdated`.

identifier.description: The value of its property with the meaning `identifier` (an ID from another source such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none. The property itself stays under `properties`.

status.description: The status key as written; left out when the element has none (a type without status, #306).

text.description: Markdown text below the frontmatter, without the blank line after the closing `---` (ADR-0004). Left out by list commands unless asked for.

version.description: The current version of the element (ADR-0005). Left out when it cannot be computed (its file no longer holds the element, an embedded image cannot be read, a counted value has no normal form); then `problems` says why (file.faulty).

versionDate.description: Date of the version from Git (D-013: shown instead of the hash; ADR-0005): the committer date of the newest commit that started this version (no parent of it had the version), in UTC as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. null when no commit has it (uncommitted content), when Git cannot tell (no git, not a repository, no commit, shallow clone) and when Git did not answer in time. Left out when `version` is left out.

readOnly.description: Unknown type, invalid metamodel or read-only repository (SR-011 AK3, SR-016 AK3, SR-018 AK2).

validity.description: Given by data.export: the UUIDs of the variants the property with the meaning `validity` names, in its order; `[]` = the core and every variant (SR-040 AK1, D-020). Left out when the metamodel has no validity property.

packages.description: Given by data.export: the UUIDs of the packages the property with the meaning `packages` names, in its order; `[]` when none. Left out when the metamodel has no packages property.

emergent.description: SR-035: true when the element's property with the meaning `emergent` holds the choice `yes` (assumption, spec question #591); only true is given, left out otherwise. An emergent requirement is never `indirect`: without an own verification record in a view it is `open` there.

properties.description: All other properties by key, unknown ones included.

relations.description: The element's own relations, then the targets of its properties of kind `relation` (`property: true`), then the incoming relations (`direction: in`); in stage 1 only the relations with the meaning `replacement` from the successors of an element with a status marked invalid (SR-072 AK3). The targets of `validity` and `packages` also appear in `validity` and `packages` in data.export. `currentVersion` and `outdated` are given by data.export and trace.matrix.

verification.description: Verification status per view: core and each variant the element is valid for (SR-047 AK3).

validation.description: SR-038: the Validierungsstatus from the validation records of the core (no `variant`) against the element's current version; the newest record of that version decides, only records of older versions give `outdated`. Given for every element whose type has the meaning `need` (`open` without record) and for every other element with a validation record; left out otherwise (assumption, spec question #534). Never inherited from children; never the element's `status` (D-030).

kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation` (e.g. `validity`, `packages`) that stores the target; such a property's targets also stay under `properties` as stored, and their entries have `property: true` and no `meaning`.

property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind (ADR-0004). Left out for relation kinds.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the other end (#416): the one the relation names, the source's own when it names none; for `direction: in` the source's (the other end: a successor, or the source of any incoming relation). Given in every `targetState`, as the name it stores for `inaccessible` and `unknown-repository`; left out only when the stored `repository` is not text. With `id` it names the target (`element.get` with `ref` and `repository`, SR-088; an `ambiguous` target also needs `file`; for `unknown-repository` the name is not a repository of the workspace).

shortId.description: Of the other end when it is available; of a target in a repository that is not on this machine with the prefix `UNKNOWN`, since its type is not known (SR-006 AK1, spec question #154).

identifier.description: Identifier of the other end (#305), only when it is available locally and has one.

title.description: Only when the other end is available locally, also across repositories, where the file stores no title (SR-005 AK2, SR-006 AK1).

targetState.description: Where the other end is (D-058): `available` = exactly one element with the UUID in the repository the relation names (the source's own when it names none); `inaccessible` = that repository is in the workspace file but not on this machine (N-041, SR-006); `missing` = the repository is here, the UUID is not in it (N-065, SR-089); `ambiguous` = several files there share the UUID (SR-088); `unknown-repository` = the workspace file lists no repository of that name, or `repository` is not text.

evidenceRecord.description: An evidence record (Datensatz) as commands return it (SR-024 AK4, SR-028): the fields of `evidence-record.schema.json` with the same rules, from a Markdown record or a JUnit test case alike, without the format marker `logreq-record`; `test-case` is `testCase`.

element.description: Verification: a requirement. Validation: a need or a requirement (D-012).

variant.description: Variant the record holds for. Absent: the core (D-026, SR-047 AK2).

item.description: Prüfling. Required for verification, optional for validation (D-007).

evidence.description: Where the Beleg is: relative path, file URL or any URI.

testCase.description: Optional test case name or ID (D-026, SR-033): the `test-case` of a Markdown record, the `name` of a JUnit test case.

source.description: The format of the record file: a Markdown record (`evidence-record.schema.json`) or a test case of a JUnit XML file (ADR-0012).

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the record file (an evidence location of the workspace file).

file.description: The record file, relative to its repository, `/` as separator.

line.description: The line of the `<testcase>` in a JUnit file; 1 for a Markdown record.

className.description: The `classname` of a JUnit test case; with `testCase` it names the test case (ADR-0012). Left out for a Markdown record.

baselines.description: The `name` of every baseline file (`baseline.schema.json`, in the `baselines` folder of the workspace file) that lists the element of the record with its version (SR-032 AK2), in file order, each name once. Only `evidence.list` fills it.

testCase.description: A test case (SR-033) seen from one element: the test case named by JUnit `classname` and `name`, or by the `test-case` of Markdown records (ADR-0012), with the records of that one element. Every `<testcase>` of a JUnit file and every Markdown record is one execution (Durchführung): a file that holds the test case twice (a rerun) gives two. A test case that names several elements (SR-033 AK2) is listed at each of them, each time with that element's records only, since the version and so whether a record is outdated belong to the element. A test case whose only appearances are skipped JUnit test cases (`<skipped>` gives no record) has `executed: false` and no executions (SR-033 AK3).

name.description: The JUnit `name`, or the `test-case` of the Markdown records.

className.description: The JUnit `classname`; left out for a test case of Markdown records.

elements.description: Every element the test case names, in any of its executions and skipped appearances, each once (SR-033 AK2).

executed.description: The test case has at least one record of this element (SR-033 AK3).

executions.description: The records of this element from this test case, newest first (by `date`, then repository, file and line); empty when `executed` is false.

last.description: The newest execution, `executions[0]` (SR-126 AK1); left out when `executed` is false.

verificationEntry.description: The verification status of a requirement in one view (SR-031, SR-034, SR-047 AK3): `element` `verification` gives one per view, `trace.matrix` one for its view (SR-126).

missingChildren.description: SR-034 AK2: for a requirement without own verification record in the view whose status is `open`: its counted children (derivation children whose type has the meaning `requirement`, whose status is not marked invalid and that apply in the view) that are `open`, `failed` or `outdated`; direct children only, in child order, each UUID once (twins in several repositories, SR-088, share one); left out when there is none.

verificationDegree.description: SR-037: the Nachweisgrad of a selection in one view. Counted are the requirements of the selection (type with the meaning `requirement`) whose status the metamodel does not mark invalid (AK3, D-044) and that have a verification status in the view (spec question #592).

share.description: (verified + indirect) / total (AK1, AK2), unrounded; left out when total is 0. Shown as a percentage rounded down to one decimal (ADR-0012).

counts.description: How many counted requirements have each verification status (AK1); indirect apart from verified (AK2); they add up to total.

element.title: Element file frontmatter
element.description: YAML frontmatter of an element file (D-015, D-056). The Markdown text follows the closing `---`. Only `id`, `type` and `status` are structural (`status` only for a type with statuses, #306); every other key is a property or relation kind key from the metamodel (D-043). Keys the metamodel does not know are kept unchanged and reported as hints (D-012, SR-016). See docs/adr/0004-element-file-format.md. File name: type prefix, dash, last 12 hex characters of the UUID, never changed (D-056). Value kinds are checked against the metamodel, not by this schema, so any value of an unknown key is kept (SR-016); `$defs/value` describes the values LogReq writes.

status.description: Status key from the metamodel, one of the statuses of the element's type (#306). Left out for a type without status. Only ever set by a person (D-030, SR-017).

normal-form.description: Reserved. Never written; the normal-form version is part of every stored version string (D-027).

inputValue.description: Property value as a caller gives it to element.create or element.update: like `value`, but relation targets need only `id` (and `repository` across repositories); the tool sets their version (SR-021).

value.description: Property value (text, number, date as YYYY-MM-DD, choice key, list) or relation targets. Which one is expected comes from the metamodel; a mismatch is a hint, not a parse error (SR-012 AK3).

evidence-record.title: Evidence record (Datensatz), Markdown frontmatter
evidence-record.description: Open format for a verification or validation record (D-007, D-026, SR-028). A manual record is a Markdown file with this frontmatter; the text below may describe the check. Automatic test results stay JUnit XML; the same fields are JUnit properties, see docs/adr/0012-evidence-records.md. The evidence itself (Beleg) stays where it is; `evidence` only points to it. Records written by LogReq (SR-030) and by anyone else count the same.

kind.description: Nachweis or Validierung (D-007). Validation counts only for the validation status (SR-030 AK3).

element.description: Verification: a requirement. Validation: a need or a requirement (D-012).

variant.description: Variant the record holds for. Absent: the core (D-026, SR-047 AK2).

item.description: Prüfling: the concrete build or sample that was checked. Required for verification, optional for validation (D-007).

evidence.description: Where the Beleg is: relative path, file URL or any URI. LogReq does not open or manage it.

test-case.description: Optional test case name or ID (D-026, SR-033).

filter.title: Saved filter file
filter.description: A named filter saved as YAML in the repository (D-056, SR-070): a `*.yaml` file directly in the `filters` folder of the workspace file. The same condition language is the `where` of every command that takes a selection, so a saved filter gives the same elements in app, CLI, API and MCP (SR-070 AK3). Element references may take any form (`resolveRef`); `filter.save` writes UUIDs.

view.description: Elements that apply in this view; also the view of its `verification` conditions without `variant`.

sort.description: Order of `element.list` when its input gives no `sort`.

name.description: Name of a saved filter, unique in the workspace ignoring case (spec-frage #363); used to call it (`selection.filter`). Saving under an existing name replaces that filter.

condition.description: Combinable condition (SR-069). Exactly one operator per object. `all`: every condition holds (`[]` holds), `any`: some holds (`[]` does not), `not`: it does not hold.

type.description: Type keys; an element of a subtype matches too unless `subtypes` is false.

subtypes.description: Include subtypes of the type. Absent means true.

status.description: Status keys as written in the files.

validFor.description: Elements that apply in this view by their validity.

verification.description: Verification status in `variant`, else in the view of the selection, else in the core.

validation.description: Needs always (open without record), other elements only with a validation record (assumption #534).

emergent.description: true: the property with the meaning `emergent` is `yes`; false: it is not.

source.description: Value of the property with meaning `source` of imported elements.

text.description: Elements that element.search finds for this query (SR-068): every word in the title, text, a property value, the type or status name, or an ID, typo tolerant, in any case. A query without a word matches none.

propertyCondition.description: Condition on the values of any property: none when it is absent, `null` or `[]`, else the items of a list or the one value. `exists`: some value, `missing`: none (both without `value`). `eq`: some value equals `value` (1 is not "1"), `ne`: not `eq`, `in`: some value equals an item of the list `value`. `contains`: some text contains `value`, ignoring case. `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`: numbers with numbers, texts with texts by code units (ISO dates compare as dates). `matches`: some text matches the JavaScript regular expression `value` (flag u). A choice may be given by its display name. A key that holds relations takes element references, with `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `exists` and `missing` only.

relationCondition.description: Condition on relations, e.g. without child: {relation: {meaning: derivation, direction: down}, exists: false} (SR-069 AK3). Evidence is a relation direction too. `exists: true` without `to` counts a relation also when its target is not available; with `to`, only an available other end that meets it.

kind.description: A relation kind or a property of kind relation (validity, packages); with `meaning`, the kind must have it.

meaning.description: Every relation kind with this meaning. Neither `kind` nor `meaning`: every relation kind.

direction.description: `up` = outgoing (to parents), `down` = incoming (from children), `evidence` = verification records pointing at the element in the view of the selection, else in the core (a record without variant holds for the core, one with a variant for that variant), of any version and result; validation records do not count (D-007); no `kind`, `meaning` or `to`. Absent: up or down.

to.description: Condition the other end must meet.

sortKey.description: Sort by a property, the short ID, or the derivation hierarchy (SR-075). Nothing about order is ever stored in element files.

by.description: `id`: short ID. `identifier`: the identifier property (meaning `identifier`, e.g. SR-36), digit runs by number (SR-9 before SR-10; ascending: elements without one follow by short ID; `desc` reverses; shadows a property named `identifier`). `type`, `status`: metamodel order. `title`: the title property. `hierarchy`: the derivation tree, ascending only. Else a property key (not one that holds relations), by its first value: choices in metamodel order, then numbers, texts (ignoring case), booleans; no value last in both orders.

metamodel.title: Metamodel file
metamodel.description: One YAML file of the metamodel (D-021, D-056, SR-011). A metamodel is all *.yaml files in the metamodel folder named in the workspace file; their lists are merged, and every key must be unique across all files. Keys never change; names may (D-043, SR-015). Built-in meanings (D-012) are attached with `meaning`. A type or property meaning is assigned to at most one key, counting only the `meaning` a definition sets itself and would not inherit anyway; a second key is a metamodel error (SR-013, SR-014 AK3); several relation kinds may share a relation meaning, e.g. Refines and Derives from are both `derivation` (D-012). A type inherits the meaning of the type it extends unless it sets its own.

name.description: Display name. English in the standard model (D-019).

prefix.description: Prefix of the short ID, e.g. SR (D-017). UNKNOWN is reserved for elements of an unknown type and is a metamodel error (#154).

extends.description: Parent type; its properties and required properties are inherited, over any number of levels (SR-012 AK2). A parent that is not defined, or a cycle, is a metamodel error.

abstract.description: No elements of this type can be created; only for inheritance.

properties.description: Property keys this type has, in addition to inherited ones, which come first. Each should be a defined property; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and the type is treated as not having it (#141 c).

required.description: Mandatory property keys (Pflichtfelder), in addition to inherited ones; each is also a property of the type and should be a defined property; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and the type is treated as not having it (#141 c). Empty values are allowed but give a hint (SR-064).

statuses.description: Status keys elements of this type may have, in addition to inherited ones (#306): the top-level `statuses` stay the vocabulary (names, `invalid`, `initial`), a type only restricts it. Left out on the type and on every ancestor: every status. Once the type or any ancestor has a list, only the listed statuses count: a type with a list below a parent without one has only its own statuses (an unrestricted parent does not add every status). An empty list on a type whose ancestors have none: the type has no status, and its element files have no `status`. Each should be a defined status; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and left out (when no key is left, the type has no status). A type whose statuses are all marked invalid (e.g. `[retired]`) has an optional status (#344): its elements without status are current, element.create gives them none, and element.supersede retires them. A status outside the list gives a hint on the element (`element.status-not-allowed`).

typeMeaning.description: Built-in meaning of the type (D-012): `requirement` (target of verification), `need` (may be validated), `variant` (D-020), `package` (D-040).

effectiveType.description: A type with its inheritance resolved (SR-012), as metamodel.get returns it; never written in a file. Key, name, description, prefix and extends are as written in the type's definition.

abstract.description: Not inherited: a type is abstract only when its own definition says so.

ancestors.description: The parent, its parent and so on, up to the root type.

properties.description: All property keys of the type, each once: those of the root type first, then down to the type itself (the key order of new keys in element files, ADR-0004). Required keys count as properties. Keys that no property definition has are left out (#141 c).

required.description: All required property keys, own and inherited, in the same order. Keys that no property definition has are left out (#141 c).

statuses.description: The status keys elements of the type may have, own and inherited, in the order of the metamodel's statuses (#306): every status when neither the type nor an ancestor has `statuses`; empty when the type has no status. Keys that no status definition has are left out.

meaning.description: Own meaning, else the meaning of the closest ancestor that has one.

target-types.description: Allowed target types, for kind `relation`: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it, SR-086).

content.description: Part of the content and therefore of the version (D-013). Title and status are never content.

markdown.description: Values are Markdown like the text: emphasis, code and inline references `[label](logreq:<uuid>?version=...)`, which are followed, checked and confirmed like those in the text (SR-127). Only for kind `text`, and never with the meaning `title` or `identifier`. It does not change the version of an element (ADR-0005); images in such a value are no embedded images.

propertyMeaning.description: Built-in meaning (D-012, D-059): `title`; `validity` (list of variants, D-020); `packages` (D-040); `emergent` (emergent behaviour, N-010; a choice without `many` whose key `yes` is the mark, SR-035; otherwise a warning and nothing is marked); `verification-method`; `statement` (Stellungnahme for ReqIF, SR-058); `source`, `source-identifier`, `import-date`, `delivery` (origin of imported elements, written only by ReqIF import, SR-057); `identifier` (an ID from another source, such as the spec ID SR-036 or a customer ID, D-017; unique per type; element references accept it besides the UUID and short ID, and outputs show it next to the short ID, #305). A property with the meaning `identifier` is of kind `text` without `many`.

relationKind.description: Relation kind (Beziehungsart). Stored under its key in the source file. `source-types`/`target-types` restrict where it may be set (SR-012 AK4, SR-067).

inverse-name.description: Name shown at the target, e.g. Derived by.

source-types.description: Allowed source types: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it, SR-086).

target-types.description: Allowed target types: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it, SR-086).

relationMeaning.description: Built-in meaning (D-012, D-059). `derivation`: source is child, target is parent (chain, coverage, indirect verification). `replacement`: source replaces target, either for the variants in the source's validity (D-020) or, when the target has an invalid status, as its successor (D-045, SR-072). `exclusion`: source variant excludes target core requirement, written in the variant file (SR-042, D-059). Without meaning a relation has no traceability semantics.

invalid.description: Elements with this status do not count for coverage, verification degree and indirect verification, but stay visible in chains (D-044).

initial.description: Status of new elements. Exactly one status is initial. A type whose statuses do not include it gives its new elements its first status that is not marked invalid, in metamodel order, and so does every type when the initial status is marked invalid (a metamodel warning, #350); a type without status or with only invalid statuses gives them none (#306, #344).

recent-workspaces.title: Recent workspaces file
recent-workspaces.description: `recent-workspaces.json` in `<OS cache>/logreq/` (ADR-0008): the workspaces the app opened last (SR-131), the most recent first, at most 20, one per folder. The app's core process records the root of every workspace it opens; the app's main process reads the list for "Open workspace". It is internal and private (mode 0600, like `api.json`), holds absolute paths of the user's workspaces and nothing else, and lies outside every working tree. Removing it only forgets the list.

workspaces.description: The most recent first; no two entries with the same `key`.

workspace.description: One workspace that was opened: its root, its canonical name and when it was opened last.

root.description: The absolute path of the workspace root as it was opened last (the folder that holds `logreq-workspace.yaml`); shown, and opened as it is.

key.description: The canonical root (absolute, symbolic links resolved, lower case on Windows), computed when the workspace was opened: two names of one folder are one entry. Never resolved again on reading.

reqif-mapping.title: ReqIF mapping file
reqif-mapping.description: Mapping of the types and attributes of one ReqIF source to the own metamodel, saved as YAML in the repository and reused for every later import from and export to that source (N-045, D-022, SR-054). The own metamodel is never changed by it (SR-054 AK3). Also holds saved export profiles (SR-059 AK3).

name.description: Name of the source as written to the property with meaning `source` (SR-057, D-059).

tool-id.description: REQ-IF-TOOL-ID seen in deliveries, for recognising the source.

target.description: Folder where imported elements are written.

source.description: LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE.

source-type.description: Restricts the entry to one SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE.

source.description: LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the ATTRIBUTE-DEFINITION.
LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the SPEC-RELATION-TYPE.

statement.description: Where the statement (Stellungnahme) goes when exporting back to the source (SR-058).

property.description: Own property that holds the statement.

workspace-local.title: Local workspace overrides
workspace-local.description: `.logreq/local.yaml` next to `logreq-workspace.yaml`: settings of one person on one machine. The file is not committed (add `.logreq/` to `.gitignore`). It overrides where a repository of the workspace lies locally (SR-004). Faulty content is reported as a warning and ignored.

repositories.description: Per repository name of the workspace file: where it lies on this machine.

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the main repository (the folder with `logreq-workspace.yaml`). No `~` expansion.

workspace.title: Workspace file
workspace.description: `logreq-workspace.yaml` in the root of the main repository (D-041, SR-004). Names the repositories that belong together. Everyone has locally only those they may access; missing ones are shown as not available (N-041, SR-004 AK3). A single-repository workspace lists only itself (SR-004 AK2).

repositories.description: The entry with `main: true` is the repository that holds this file. With two or more repositories exactly one has `main: true`; a single repository is the main one even without it. Names are unique (checked by LogReq; JSON Schema cannot express it).

metamodel.description: Where the metamodel lies: a folder in one of the repositories, the main one or its own (D-021, SR-011, SR-018).

evidence.description: Folders with evidence records (Markdown) and JUnit XML files (SR-028 AK1). They may be in repositories of other tools.

baselines.description: Where new baseline files are written. Default: folder `baselines` in the main repository.

filters.description: Where saved filters are written (SR-070). Default: folder `filters` in the main repository.

mappings.description: Where ReqIF mapping files are written (SR-054). Default: folder `reqif` in the main repository.

ignore.description: Glob patterns of paths that are never read as elements, relative to each repository and anchored at its root, with `/` as separator (no `\`, no `//`). `*` matches any characters within one name, `?` one character, `**` as a whole name any number of names, including none; every other character is literal (no `[...]`, no `{a,b}`). Case-sensitive on every OS; wildcards match names starting with `.`. A leading `/` or `./` and a trailing `/` are dropped; `x/**` matches folder `x` itself, so it is skipped as a whole. Example: `website/**`, `**/*.draft.md`. `.git` and `node_modules` are always ignored.

url.description: Address of the repository on the Git server. Informational: LogReq never clones or fetches (D-036).

path.description: Expected local location relative to the main repository, with `/` as separator. Default `../<name>`; always `.` for the main repository. Absolute paths and `\` are warned about (an absolute path is ignored); there is no `~` expansion. A person can override it in the untracked file `.logreq/local.yaml`.

tools.name: workspace_init
tools.title: Initialise workspace
tools.description: Create a workspace with the standard model in an existing folder.

path.description: Existing folder; must not contain logreq-workspace.yaml or the metamodel file.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: workspace_status
tools.title: Show workspace status
tools.description: Repositories of the workspace, which are available, where the metamodel comes from, read-only state.

readOnly.description: LogReq cannot write the repository folder itself (read-only file system or no write permission). Reading works as usual and the workspace stays writable; writes into this repository are refused with file.read-only (SR-018 AK2). Rights on the Git server are not visible here (D-016, D-024). Only for available repositories; left out where the operating system cannot tell (Windows).

tools.name: workspace_check
tools.title: Check workspace
tools.description: Check the whole workspace against the metamodel: files, required and unknown properties, statuses outside the type and missing statuses, missing targets, cycles, duplicate IDs, outdated relations, evidence records that cannot be read or name an unknown element. ok is false, and the CLI exits 1, on findings at or above failOn (default error).

changedFiles.description: Restrict the check to the elements in these files and their targets (SR-092). A file must lie in a repository of the workspace and be no folder; deleted and non-element files add nothing. With changedSince, both count. To cover deleted elements, use changedSince: a deleted file named only in changedFiles adds no old UUID.

changedSince.description: Git revision, e.g. the target commit of a merge request: restrict the check to the elements whose files (or embedded images) in the working copy differ from it, untracked files included, and their targets (SR-092). Looked up in every repository of the workspace; a repository without it, or without Git, adds nothing and gets an info problem (git.revision-missing, git.unavailable). The relations to an element file deleted since, or whose UUID changed, are kept. Error git.commit-not-found (CLI exit code 4) when no repository has it.

severity.description: Lowest severity of the problems shown; does not change ok or the exit code. Findings left out are counted in hidden.

failOn.description: Lowest severity of a finding that makes ok false (CLI exit code 1), shown or not; independent of severity. With the default, warnings and info never fail the check.

ok.description: False when the workspace has a finding at or above failOn, shown or not (CLI exit code 1, ADR-0009). In a restricted check, of the findings the restriction keeps.

hidden.description: The findings that severity leaves out of problems, by severity; only when it leaves out at least one, so that no problems shown does not read as no findings.

below.description: The severity given: the findings counted are below it.

checkedElements.description: Number of elements checked: all of the workspace, or in a restricted check the changed elements and their targets (SR-092).

durationMs.description: Time the check took in milliseconds. Not given yet: it differs between calls, and the cross-access test compares outputs (SR-080 AK2).

tools.name: workspace_activity
tools.title: Show last agent access
tools.description: The element read or changed last through the local API or the MCP server on this working copy: which access, command and effect, when, and the element (UUID, repository); null when none is recorded.

activity.description: The last call through the API or the MCP server that named one element (the element reference it was given, or else the one element file a write wrote), as an API or MCP process of this copy recorded it in the cache folder of the copy (ADR-0008). null when there is none, the copy has no usable cache folder, or the record cannot be read. Calls of the command line and of the app are not recorded.

tools.name: workspace_recent
tools.title: List recent workspaces
tools.description: The workspaces the app opened last, the most recent first (at most 20): the root of each, when it was opened, and whether the root still holds logreq-workspace.yaml. The list belongs to the user, not to a workspace, so every access gives the same list from any folder.

root.description: The absolute path of the workspace root as the app opened it last (the folder that holds logreq-workspace.yaml).

opened.description: When the app opened it last.

exists.description: Whether `<root>/logreq-workspace.yaml` is a file now: the root itself, never a folder above it. A root without an answer within 1 s (a share that does not answer) counts as false.

workspaces.description: The workspaces the app opened last, the most recent first, as the app's core process recorded them in `<OS cache>/logreq/recent-workspaces.json` (ADR-0008). Empty when none is recorded or the list cannot be read. Only the app records; the command line, the API and the MCP server only read the list.

tools.name: metamodel_get
tools.title: Show metamodel
tools.description: The effective metamodel: types with inherited properties and statuses, properties, relation kinds, statuses, meanings.

types.description: The types with inheritance resolved (SR-012), in metamodel order; `statuses` are the statuses each type offers (#306).

meanings.description: Every built-in meaning of metamodel.schema.json (`meaning` of types, properties and relation kinds) -> the keys whose own definition declares it, in metamodel order; empty if unassigned (SR-013 AK3). In a valid metamodel a type or property meaning has at most one key, a relation meaning any number. Types that inherit a meaning, or repeat the one they inherit, are not listed; `types` shows their effective `meaning`.

tools.name: element_create
tools.title: Create element
tools.description: Create an element with a new random UUID. Only title, text and required properties are needed; empty required properties give a hint (SR-064). New elements always get the initial status of the metamodel (D-030); when their type lacks it or it is marked invalid, the first status of the type in metamodel order that is not marked invalid, and no status for a type without status or with only invalid statuses (#306, #344).

text.description: Markdown text of the element, written below the frontmatter after one blank line; that blank line after the closing `---` is not part of the text. A final line break is added (ADR-0004).

folder.description: Folder relative to the repository; default from the type.

tools.name: element_get
tools.title: Get element
tools.description: One element with text, properties, relations, version (and on request its date), hints, and which variants replace or exclude it.

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the version (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005), read from the Git history. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out, so opening an element stays fast (SR-082 AK3); the app asks for the date in a second call.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; #255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.description: Text, properties, version and, with the input `versionDate`, its date (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005: the committer date in UTC of the newest commit that started this version; null for content no commit has and when Git cannot tell, including a git call that timed out; left out without the input), the own relations, the successors of a superseded element (SR-072 AK3), the hints of the element (none while the metamodel is not valid; also `variant.superseded-in-validity`, SR-040 AK3, the outdated relations and inline references of the element, `relation.outdated`, SR-026 AK3, whose messages name the dates of both versions only with the input `versionDate`, and `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no property has the meaning title) and `readOnly`, always given (unknown type, invalid metamodel or a repository folder that cannot be written). An element with a value that counts and has no normal form (`.inf`, `.nan`, ADR-0005) comes without `version` and `versionDate`, with a `file.faulty` warning last in its hints that says why (#276). The incoming relations of every kind: `trace.neighbourhood` with `direction: down`. `verification`, for an element whose type has the meaning `requirement`: its verification status in the core and in each variant it applies in, as evidence.status gives it (SR-031), with the indirect verification and the children that are missing (SR-034). `validation`: its validation status (SR-038), for every need and for any other element with a validation record, separate from `verification`. The variants that replace or exclude the element (SR-046, stage 5) have no field in the schema yet; they come with that stage.

fileSha256.description: Of the file this answer was read from, for expectedFileSha256 of element.update (SR-106).

tools.name: element_resolve
tools.title: Resolve reference
tools.description: Resolve a reference from another tool (UUID, short ID or identifier, optional version) and tell whether the version is current.

version.description: The version the reference stores (D-013); optional. A version of another normal form than the one the tool computes (n1) is refused with input.invalid (ADR-0005).

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the current version (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005), read from the Git history, as element.get does with the same input. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; #255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.description: The element as element.get shows it, with title, text, status, current version (SR-060 AK1), verification status (SR-031, SR-034) and validation status (SR-038) and, with the input `versionDate`, the date of that version (as element.get gives it; left out without the input). Without a version (a value that counts has no normal form) `version` and `versionDate` are left out and the hints end with a `file.faulty` warning, as in element.get (#276). An unknown reference is the error ref.unknown, one that fits several elements ref.ambiguous with details.candidates (AK3). A short ID whose prefix fits no element stays ref.unknown, never another element; when its tail fits exactly one element of another type, details.candidates names that element and the message asks whether its short ID was meant (prefix may be outdated, #275).

current.description: Whether the given version is the element's current version, computed from its file as it is now (SR-060 AK2): "current" or "outdated"; "unknown" when the element has no version to compare with (a value that counts has no normal form, `.inf` or `.nan`, ADR-0005: `element` comes without `version` and with a `file.faulty` warning that says why, #276); null when no version was given. Strings, not booleans, so a caller that tests the field for truth never takes "unknown" for current.

tools.name: element_list
tools.title: List all elements
tools.description: Elements of a selection, sorted; optionally as derivation tree.

selection.description: Every part given must hold (SR-101 AK2).

sort.description: Keys in order: ties go to the next key, then to the workspace order (also without sort). `hierarchy` only first: the list is then the derivation tree, see `tree`. Without sort, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`.

withText.description: Also give the text of each element. Left out for an element without a version, and when its file changed while the list was built (list again).

tree.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy` (SR-075 AK2): the place in the derivation tree of each element of `elements`, in the same order. The list is the tree depth first: each root, then the elements below it. Each element of the selection appears once (spec-frage #354): below the parent of the list that reaches it at the shortest depth, the first in sort order among equals; an element without a parent in the list is a root, and so is the first element in sort order of a cycle that no root reaches. Its other parents are in its `relations`.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

depth.description: 0 for a root, 1 for an element below it, and so on.

parent.description: The element it is shown below, a parent of it by a derivation; left out for a root. It may lie on an earlier page.

tools.name: element_facets
tools.title: Show facets
tools.description: Types, statuses and property values of the elements of a selection, with counts, to choose a filter from.

selection.description: Every part given must hold (SR-101 AK2). Without it, every element.

maxValues.description: A property of kind text, number or date gives its values only when it has at most this many distinct values in the whole workspace and at least one of them is shared by two elements; otherwise it is free text, found with element.search (SR-068). Choice and relation properties always give their values.

types.description: The types of the selected elements as written in the files, with the number of elements of exactly this type (an element of a subtype is not counted under its parent): types of the metamodel in metamodel order with their name, then other type keys in store order (name = key). Types without a selected element are not listed (SR-118).

statuses.description: The statuses of the selected elements as written in the files, with the number of elements: statuses of the metamodel in metamodel order, then other values in store order. Elements without status are not counted.

properties.description: Every property that a type of a selected element has, in the order of the property definitions of the metamodel. Keys no type has (SR-016) are not listed. The counts and values are those of all selected elements, as the filter conditions read them (any type, SR-069): an element whose type lacks the property counts by the value its file holds (usually none).

count.description: Selected elements that have some value.

missing.description: Selected elements that have no value (absent, null or []); the elements `{ property, op: "missing" }` selects.

distinct.description: Distinct values the property can be filtered on (for a relation property: distinct available targets). Free text without values counts only up to maxValues + 1, see distinctCapped.

distinctCapped.description: Only for free text: there are more distinct values than maxValues, and `distinct` stopped counting at maxValues + 1.

values.description: Left out for free text (see maxValues). Choices: in metamodel order, then other values as written. Relation targets: by title ignoring case, then short ID. Others: numbers ascending, then texts ignoring case, then booleans. Each value is what a property condition takes with op eq and selects exactly the elements counted: for a relation target its short ID; a choice stored under a name the condition would map to another key, or one that names several choices, is not given. Targets that are not available are left out (a condition cannot name them).

count.description: Selected elements that have this value.

title.description: Title of a relation target; left out when it has none.

identifier.description: Identifier of a relation target, when it has one.

tools.name: element_update
tools.title: Update element
tools.description: Change title, text or properties of one element. Unknown properties are kept; status changes only via element.setStatus.

text.description: New Markdown text of the element; the blank line after the closing `---` is not part of the text, so the text element.get gives can be passed back unchanged. A changed text gets a final line break (ADR-0004).

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; #255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

expectedFileSha256.description: Write precondition (SR-106): the fileSha256 the change was made on. If the file has other bytes now, nothing is written: file.changed-on-disk, also when nothing would change.

fileSha256.description: Of the file as written, or as read when nothing changed (SR-106).

affected.description: The number of directly affected elements (SR-024 AK2): the distinct elements other than this one whose files hold a relation or an inline reference to it, the elements at distance 1 of `trace.affected`. Counted only when the save changed the version (the content, D-013); 0 when only the title or properties that do not count to the version changed, or nothing changed (SR-024 AK3). For an element without a version (a value that counts has no normal form, ADR-0005) what the version is computed from is compared, so a save of only its title or status also gives 0 (#276).

tools.name: element_setStatus
tools.title: Set status
tools.description: Set or remove the status of elements on explicit request of the caller. Only a status of each element's type is taken (`statuses` of the type in metamodel.get, #306); an element of a type without status gets none. `status: null` removes the status line where the type's status is optional (#343). The only command besides element.supersede that changes a status; no command changes a status on its own (D-030, SR-087).

status.description: Key or display name of a status of the metamodel, in any case; the key is written. It must be a status of the element's type (#306). null removes the status line, only from an element whose type has an optional status: no status, or only statuses marked invalid (#343); else input.invalid with reason status-required.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: element_supersede
tools.title: Supersede element
tools.description: Supersede an element: set an invalid status of its type and optionally let a successor replace it (relation with meaning replacement, written into the successor's file). There is no delete (D-045).

status.description: Key or display name of a status of the metamodel, in any case; the key is written. It must be a status of the element's type that the metamodel marks invalid (#306).

relation.description: Relation kind with meaning replacement to write from the successor; needed only when more than one fits the types and the successor does not already have the relation under exactly one of them.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: element_bulkUpdate
tools.title: Bulk update elements
tools.description: Set, add to or remove one property for all elements of a selection. Without `confirm` only previews: the number of affected elements and the skipped ones, whose type does not have the property. With `confirm` writes only that property's lines (SR-102). Never id, type or status (element.setStatus takes several refs).

property.description: A property of the metamodel; not the title key, not a relation kind.

operation.description: set: replace the value. add: append the items an element does not hold yet (a property with many). remove: without value the property, with value these items (many).

value.description: For set and add. A choice by key or name; relation targets as for element.update.

confirm.description: Write the change; without it nothing is written. A written file also gets the current titles of its same-repository relation targets (decision on #307), which the preview does not show.

expected.description: The count of the preview: with confirm, refused (nothing written) when the change now affects another number of elements.

applied.description: True when the files were written (confirm).

affected.description: The elements whose file the change rewrites, in store order.

unchanged.description: Elements of the selection that have the result already.

skipped.description: Elements left out because the metamodel does not allow the property for them (SR-071 AK3).

files.description: Written files relative to the workspace root; empty in a preview.

problems.description: Hints at the property in the affected elements after the change: value kind (SR-085), target types (SR-086).

tools.name: element_addAttachment
tools.title: Add attachment
tools.description: Copy an image into the folder named like the element file, next to it, and return the Markdown that embeds it relatively; once the text embeds it, the image counts to the version (SR-097, D-057). Never replaces a file.

sourcePath.description: The image to copy: a file ending in .avif, .bmp, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .svg or .webp (any case).

file.description: The image file relative to the workspace root, / as separator, e.g. requirements/SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png. Its name is the source name with only ASCII letters, digits, _ and -, and -2, -3, ... when the folder has that name already; a file there with the same bytes is reused.

markdown.description: The image as Markdown with a link relative to the element file, e.g. ![layout](SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png), to insert into the text and save with element.update.

tools.name: relation_options
tools.title: Show relation options
tools.description: Relation kinds the metamodel allows from an element, each with the types its target may have (SR-067); search a target with element.search and selection.where: { type: targetTypes }.

ref.description: The element that gets the relation (its source).

kind.description: Only this relation kind: none when the type of the element does not allow it.

kinds.description: In metamodel order: every relation kind whose source-types allow the type of the element (subtypes count) and whose target-types allow some type; none for an element of a type the metamodel does not know (SR-016 AK3). These are the kinds relation.add accepts.

name.description: Display name of the relation kind.

targetTypes.description: Every type of the metamodel a target may have, subtypes included, in metamodel order; relation.add refuses a target of another known type.

tools.name: relation_add
tools.title: Create relation
tools.description: Add a relation; stores target UUID and current version, plus the title only within the same repository.

tools.name: relation_remove
tools.title: Remove relation
tools.description: Remove a relation from the source file.

repository.description: Only relations into this repository (workspace name); a relation that names none points into the source's repository (D-058). Names the one meant when a UUID has relations into several repositories.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: trace_chain
tools.title: Show trace chain
tools.description: Chain up to the top parents and down to evidence, with depth, gaps and cycles; one page of nodes at a time, total counts all.

limit.description: Nodes of the page; total counts all. The walk is always complete: depth, gaps, cycles and incomplete are those of the whole chain (spec-frage #290). Every page walks the whole chain again; to step through a chain, ask with `maxDepth` instead.

offset.description: Nodes skipped before the page, in the order of `nodes` (the root, then the parents level by level, then the children level by level).

nodes.description: Every element of the chain once per direction, at its shortest depth (SR-022 AK1, AK2): the root first, then the parents level by level, then the children level by level. An element reached again (a diamond, a cycle) is not repeated; its edge is in `edges` (SR-022 AK4). In a view, only the elements that apply in it (SR-040); the root always. An element is named by its UUID and `repository` (D-058); two files of one repository with the same UUID (SR-088) are two nodes, told apart only by `file`, and edges and gaps name both the same way. Only the page of `limit` nodes from `offset` (in this order) is listed; `total` counts every node. A chain can be large (in a workspace of 50,000 elements and 200,000 relations up to about 42,000 nodes): a client asks for the first page and further ones as needed (SR-082 AK4, spec-frage #290), or shows it step by step with `maxDepth` 1 and asks again below an element that is not `expanded`.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

depth.description: Steps from the root: 0 for the root, 1 for its parents or children, and so on.

direction.description: `up` for a parent (and its parents), `down` for a child (and its children); left out for the root.

expanded.description: Its parents or children were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the chain was cut.

total.description: The number of all nodes of the chain; `nodes` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

edges.description: Every derivation relation the chain followed, from the child that stores it (`source`) to its parent (`target`, ADR-0004): the upward ones, then the downward ones, in the order they were followed. Paged with the nodes: an edge is listed on the page of the node it leads to in its walk (upwards the parent, downwards the child), so every edge is on exactly one page.

sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

kind.description: Key of the relation kind with the meaning `derivation` (SR-013).

cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of derivations (SR-022 AK4).

gaps.description: The gaps of the downward chain (SR-022 AK3), in the order of `nodes`, only those of the nodes of the page: `no-child` for a need without a child, `no-evidence` for a requirement without a child and without evidence. Only for elements whose children were looked at (`expanded`). `no-evidence`: the element has no verification record in `view`, in the core without `view` (as `evidence.coverage` and the filter condition `verification`; any version and result, spec question #527 Q3), so without `view` a requirement verified only for a variant shows its records in `evidence` and still has the gap (spec question #527 Q4). A test case that was only skipped does not close the gap.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element with the gap.

evidence.description: The evidence (Nachweise) of the downward chain (SR-022 AK1, SR-033 AK1 to AK3), in the order of `nodes`, only for the nodes of the page whose children were looked at (`expanded`), paged like `gaps`; one item per element that has any, none with `direction` `up`. Only verification records (D-007: the chain ends at the Nachweise; validation records are in `evidence.list`). With `view` only the records that hold in it (SR-047: the core the records without a variant, a variant those for it); without `view` every record, each with its `variant`, as `evidence.list`. A test case all of whose executions of the element hold in another view is left out; a test case that was only skipped shows in every view. The Beleg of a record is its `evidence`; a JUnit execution has none, its Beleg is its record file (`repository`, `file`, `line`; D-007: for automatic tests the record is the result file). Belege are text and never opened.

id.description: The element of the chain the evidence belongs to.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of that element.

depth.description: The element's depth plus one: the evidence is one level below it (SR-022 AK1).

testCases.description: The test cases that name the element (SR-033), by class name, then name, each with the element's own executions newest first (`elements` names every element the test case names, SR-033 AK2); `executed` false for a test case that was only skipped (SR-033 AK3).

records.description: Unlike `evidence.list` `records`: only the element's records without a test case (inspection, analysis, demonstration, manual records without `test-case`), newest first.

unresolved.description: Derivation relations the chain could not follow (SR-006 AK1, SR-088, SR-089): upwards a parent that is not available, downwards a child whose relation points at a UUID several files of the repository share. The other end is shown by its short ID only when it is not available (prefix `UNKNOWN` when its repository is not on this machine). A parent whose `id` is no UUID is not listed (the value-kind check reports it, SR-085); in a repository that is not here it still makes the chain `incomplete`. Only those of the nodes of the page (`from`).

from.description: The element of the chain whose parents or children were looked at.

fromRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `from`.

id.description: The other end: the parent the relation names (up), the child that stores it (down).

identifier.description: Identifier of the other end (#305), when it is available and has one.

targetState.description: As in `data-export.schema.json#/$defs/relation`; downwards always `ambiguous` (the element the child points at).

incomplete.description: True when a part of the chain lies in a repository that is not on this machine (SR-006 AK2), or, when the chain goes down, an evidence location does: evidence there is not seen.

problems.description: Hints: `trace.cycle` once per cycle of derivations in the chain, naming its elements (SR-022 AK4); `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no type has the meaning `need` or `requirement`, so those gaps cannot be found (SR-013 AK3). The hints are those of the whole chain, on every page.

tools.name: trace_related
tools.title: Show related elements
tools.description: All children of a set of parents, or all parents of a set of requirements, each once, optionally up to a depth; one page at a time, total counts all.

limit.description: Elements of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Elements skipped before the page, in the order of the list (by distance from the selection).

tools.name: trace_affected
tools.title: Show affected elements
tools.description: Elements affected by a change of one element, with path and distance.

affected.description: The page of `limit` affected elements from `offset` (`total` counts all). The affected elements: every element that has a relation or an inline reference (in the text or in a property marked `markdown`, SR-127) to the element, directly or through the chain (SR-024 AK1), each once at its shortest distance, breadth first, the element itself never. Distance 1: every element whose file holds a relation (any relation kind or relation-valued property) or an inline reference to it. From there onward along the derivation chain (meaning `derivation`, SR-013) and inline references that point at an affected element.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

distance.description: Steps from the element: 1 when this element's file points at it directly.

path.description: The way: the element asked for first, this element last, each element in between that points at the one before it; each named by UUID and repository (D-058).

via.description: How this element points at the one before it on the path: a relation stored under `key` (a relation kind or a relation-valued property), or an inline reference in its text or in a property marked `markdown`.

total.description: The number of all affected elements; `affected` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

records.description: The evidence records of an older version of the element (SR-024 AK4): its records in the evidence folders (SR-028, SR-093) whose `version` is not its current one, newest first. Empty when its current version cannot be computed (its file no longer holds it, an embedded image cannot be read).

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: elements there may point at the element (SR-006 AK2).

tools.name: trace_neighbourhood
tools.title: Show neighbourhood
tools.description: The surroundings of one element over every relation kind and inline reference, up and down to a depth; each edge says whether it repeats an element and whether it is outdated. One page of nodes at a time.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get (#255).

direction.description: `up`: along the links the element's file stores (its parents, the targets of its other relations and relation properties, its inline references). `down`: along the links that point at it (its children and every element whose file has a relation or an inline reference to it). The source of a link is placed below its target (ADR-0004).

maxDepth.description: The deepest depth in each direction; 0: the root only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Walk as far as the links go (the whole chain); not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a link is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

limit.description: Nodes of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Nodes skipped before the page, in the order of `nodes` (the root, the up walk level by level, the down walk level by level).

nodes.description: Every element reached once per walk, at its shortest depth: the root, then the up walk, then the down walk, each level by level. In a view only the elements that apply in it (SR-040); the root always. Only the page of `limit` nodes from `offset` is listed; `total` counts all.

identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036, #305), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

depth.description: Steps from the root in its walk: 0 for the root.

direction.description: `up` for an element reached along the links its file stores, `down` for one reached along the links that point at it; left out for the root.

expanded.description: Its links were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the walk was cut.

total.description: The number of all nodes; `nodes` holds the page.

edges.description: Every link the walks followed, up edges first, then down edges, in walk order; an edge is on the page of the node it leads to in its walk. A hub (a package with many members) can put many edges on one page: leave out `packages` with `kinds` or `meanings`. Not listed: unresolved links (`element.get` and `workspace.check` report them).

source.description: The element whose file stores the link.

sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

target.description: The element the link points at (ADR-0004), whatever the walk direction.

targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

link.description: A relation in the frontmatter or an inline reference in the text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for an inline reference; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of the walk.

repeated.description: The edge leads, in its walk, to an element that this walk first reached through another edge, or to the root: a repetition (SR-107 AK3). It holds within one call (asking again from a child loses it; to open a tree level by level ask from the same root with a larger `maxDepth`) and within the followed kinds (the tree of derivations comes from `meanings: ["derivation"]`). First means first reached breadth first (spec question #421).

outdated.description: The link stores a version of normal form 1, its target is available and has a current version, and the two differ (SR-025).

tools.name: trace_matrix
tools.title: Show traceability matrix
tools.description: Traceability matrix of a selection: one row per element in list order, one column per relation kind and direction that occurs, each cell the elements at the other end with outdated and missing marks; per column how many rows have a link. One page of rows at a time. With evidence locations also each requirement's test cases and verification status, and the degree.

selection.description: The rows: every element the selection selects, as `element.list` selects them (every part given must hold, SR-101 AK2). In a variant view (`selection.view`, or the view of the saved filter) a link whose other end does not apply in the view is left out of the cells and the counts (SR-040), as `trace.neighbourhood` leaves it out of its walk.

sort.description: As in `element.list`: the rows are in the order `element.list` gives for the same `selection` and `sort` (SR-125 AK1). Without `sort`, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`. `hierarchy` first makes the rows the derivation tree and gives each row its `depth`.

kinds.description: Keys of the relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to make columns of. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. Without `kinds`, the columns are the relation kinds of the metamodel (Beziehungsarten, D-043, D-037): relation properties such as the package and the validity are their own built-in meanings (D-012) and form a column only when named here; inline references are no relation kind and never form a column.

limit.description: Rows of the page; `total` counts all.

offset.description: Rows skipped before the page, in the order of the list.

columns.description: One column per relation kind and direction that occurs in the whole selection (SR-125 AK2), not only on the page: a kind or direction no row has makes no column. Order: relation kinds in the order of the metamodel, then properties of kind `relation` in property order; per key `out` before `in`. `type` says what a column holds and so the shape of its cells; every column is `relation`. The evidence columns (SR-126) are no column type: their header is `evidence` and their cells are `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, so a reader of `columns` and `cells` needs no other shape.

type.description: The column holds relations: its cell in each row is an array of relations (`data-export#/$defs/relation`) of `kind` and `direction`. The evidence columns of SR-126 are `evidence`, `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, not a column type.

kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation`.

property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind.

meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

direction.description: `out`: the relations the row element's file stores. `in`: the relations of other elements that point at it.
